name: Gold Correlation Analysis: Commodities & International Assets
description: Analyzes correlations between Gold futures (GC) and a broad universe of commodities (CL, NG, SI, HG, ZW, ZC) and international assets (6E, 6J, EEM, EFA, VGK, EWJ). Outputs a pairwise correlation heatmap, 60-day rolling correlation timeseries vs gold, and a cross-sectional summary table of correlation statistics.
source:
# ============================================================================
# Gold Correlation Analysis: Commodities & International Assets
# ============================================================================
# Universe (13 assets):
#   Commodities — GC (Gold), CL (Crude Oil), NG (Nat Gas), SI (Silver),
#                 HG (Copper), ZW (Wheat), ZC (Corn)
#   FX Futures  — 6E (Euro), 6J (Japanese Yen)
#   Intl ETFs   — EEM (Emerging Mkts), EFA (MSCI EAFE), VGK (Europe), EWJ (Japan)
#
# Outputs:
#   1. Pairwise NxN correlation heatmap (all 13 assets)
#   2. 60-day rolling correlation timeseries vs Gold
#   3. Cross-sectional summary table (current, mean, min, max, all-time corr)
# ============================================================================

# ============================================================================
# DATA LOADING
# futures_continuation handles roll adjustments for all futures;
# passthrough is safe for the Stock ETFs (EEM, EFA, VGK, EWJ).
# ============================================================================
src = market_data_source(timeframe=1D)()
cont = futures_continuation(
    timeframe=1D,
    s_rollover_method=RolloverType.FirstOfMonth,
    s_adjustment_method=AdjustmentType.BackwardPanamaCanal
)(src.o, src.h, src.l, src.c, src.v, src.oi, src.s)

close = cont.c
ret   = returns(period=1)(close)

# ============================================================================
# GOLD REFERENCE (cross-sectional)
# GLD (SPDR Gold Shares) tracks GC within ~0.1% tracking error and is
# available as a cross-sectional reference series for rolling_corr inputs.
# ============================================================================
gld_ref = reference_stocks(ticker='GLD')()
gld_ret = returns(period=1)(gld_ref.c)

# ============================================================================
# ROLLING CORRELATION vs GOLD
# 60-day rolling  → captures current regime dynamics
# Expanding       → all-time relationship (ignores the fixed window parameter)
# ============================================================================
roll_corr_60d = rolling_corr(window=60,  window_type=WindowType.rolling,   method=CorrelationMethod.pearson)(x=gld_ret, y=ret)
full_corr     = rolling_corr(window=252, window_type=WindowType.expanding,  method=CorrelationMethod.pearson)(x=gld_ret, y=ret)

# ============================================================================
# OUTPUT 1 — PAIRWISE CORRELATION HEATMAP (NxN, all 13 assets)
# Pearson correlation computed automatically across the universe.
# Red / warm  = strong positive co-movement with gold.
# Blue / cool = low or negative correlation (diversifying).
# ============================================================================
cs_heatmap(
    mode=HeatmapMode.correlation,
    agg=AggregationType.Last,
    title="Pairwise Correlation Matrix — Daily Returns",
    category="1. Correlation Heatmap",
    color_axis_min=-1,
    color_axis_max=1,
    show_data_labels=True,
    data_label_format="{point.value:.2f}",
    max_assets=0
)(ret)

# ============================================================================
# OUTPUT 2 — ROLLING CORRELATION TIMESERIES (per-asset TV chart pane)
# Each asset's chart shows its own 60D rolling correlation vs Gold (GLD).
# Reference line at 0 marks the neutral boundary.
# ============================================================================
timeseries_lines(
    title="60D Rolling Correlation vs Gold",
    series=LineSeriesSchema(series=[
        LineSeriesSpec(name="60D Corr vs Gold", color=Color.Gold)
    ]),
    reference_lines=ReferenceLineSchema(lines=[
        ReferenceLine(value=0,    color=Color.Gray,  dash_style=DashStyle.Dash,  title="Zero"),
        ReferenceLine(value=0.5,  color=Color.Green, dash_style=DashStyle.Dot,   title="+0.5"),
        ReferenceLine(value=-0.5, color=Color.Red,   dash_style=DashStyle.Dot,   title="-0.5")
    ])
)(roll_corr_60d)

# ============================================================================
# OUTPUT 3 — CROSS-SECTIONAL SUMMARY TABLE
# Rows = assets; Columns = correlation statistics.
# grid_agg on each ColumnSpec overrides the global agg per column:
#   Current (60D)  → Last value of the 60D rolling series
#   Mean    (60D)  → Time-average of 60D rolling correlation
#   Min     (60D)  → Worst (most negative) 60D rolling correlation seen
#   Max     (60D)  → Highest 60D rolling correlation seen
#   All-Time       → Last value of the expanding correlation (full history)
# ============================================================================
# Pre-compute period extremes for the summary table
min_corr  = min(period=2000)(roll_corr_60d)
max_corr  = max(period=2000)(roll_corr_60d)

# ============================================================================
# OUTPUT 3 — CROSS-SECTIONAL SUMMARY TABLE
# Rows = assets; columns = key correlation statistics vs Gold.
# agg=Last takes the terminal value of each pre-computed series per asset.
#   col 1 → roll_corr_60d   : most recent 60D rolling Pearson correlation
#   col 2 → full_corr        : expanding all-time Pearson correlation
#   col 3 → min_corr         : all-time min of the 60D rolling series
#   col 4 → max_corr         : all-time max of the 60D rolling series
# ============================================================================
cs_summary_table(
    title="Correlation vs Gold — Summary Statistics",
    category="3. Summary Table",
    agg=AggregationType.Last,
    max_assets=0
)(roll_corr_60d, full_corr, min_corr, max_corr)
